Expertise

How I Can Help

Four subspecialties under one doctor, so an eye with cataract, retinal disease, corneal disease and inflammation can be planned as a whole.

Modern Imaging in the Operating Room.Dr. Thanapong is one of the pioneers of intraoperative OCT and 3D heads-up visualisation in cataract and retinal surgery. He uses these innovations in patient care to improve surgical outcomes, and teaches the techniques to surgeons across Asia-Pacific.

CATARACT & LENS

Advanced Cataract Surgery

Modern phacoemulsification with lens implants matched to how you live, from routine cataract to eyes that are harder to operate on.

  • Premium & multifocal IOLs
  • Extended depth of focus
  • Complicated cataract
  • Uveitic cataract
  • Scleral-fixated IOL
  • IOL exchange
  • RLE: Refractive Lens Exchange*
  • Weak or broken capsule

*Refractive lens exchange (RLE) is elective surgery that replaces a clear natural lens with an intraocular lens to reduce dependence on glasses. Like any intraocular surgery, it carries risks, including infection, retinal detachment (higher in highly short-sighted eyes) and glare or halos at night, which are more common with multifocal lenses. Younger patients also lose their remaining natural focusing ability. Suitability is decided only after a full eye examination and a personal discussion of the benefits and risks.

Refractive Lens Exchange

RLE: What the Guidance Says

RLE replaces a clear natural lens with an artificial one to reduce dependence on glasses. In Thailand, a 2025 practice guideline agreed by three specialist societies sets out who may be suitable and which risks to discuss.

  • Who it may suitVery high short-sight (about −8.00 D or more) or long-sight (+3.00 to +6.00 D), when laser vision correction and implantable contact lenses (ICL) are not suitable.
  • AgeGenerally avoided under 50, when the risk of retinal detachment is higher.
  • Not for reading glasses aloneRLE is not recommended to treat presbyopia on its own. An artificial lens does not match a healthy natural lens.
  • Risks to discussRetinal detachment (especially in high myopia), infection inside the eye, permanent loss of natural focusing, glare and halos at night, and capsule clouding that may need a laser.
  • Before surgeryA detailed retina examination, precise biometry and lens calculation, and an honest talk about expectations and costs.
Practice guidelineTHSCRS · June 2025 · in Thai

Practice Guideline for Refractive Lens Exchange (RLE)

Agreed by three Thai societies (cataract and refractive surgery, refraction, and cornea and refractive surgery) for the Royal College of Ophthalmologists of Thailand.

Dr. Thanapong contributed to this guideline as a member of the THSCRS committee.

Read the guideline (PDF, 5 pages)
Textbook chapterRCOPT textbook, Vol. 9 · 2025 · in Thai

Evidence-Based Medicine in Refractive Lens Exchange

Chapter 18 reviews indications, lens power calculation and lens choice, visual outcomes, and complications such as retinal detachment, with 17 references.

Co-authored by Dr. Thanapong with Dr. Thanakrit Sorasit. Dr. Thanapong also served as co-editor of the volume.

Read the chapter (PDF, 18 pages)

Both documents are in Thai and written for eye doctors. Whether RLE suits your eyes can only be decided after a full eye examination.

Before your appointment

Prepare for Your Visit

A few simple steps from booking to your first visit. Call the hospital you choose and ask for an appointment with Dr. Thanapong Somkijrungroj, Ophthalmology.

Choose a clinic
  1. Pick a clinic and day

    Weekday evenings and Saturdays at Samitivej and MedPark, or weekdays at Chulalongkorn.

  2. Call the hospital

    Give your name and say you would like to see Dr. Thanapong for cataract, retina or uveitis care.

  3. Bring your records

    Your current glasses, a list of medicines and eye drops, and any previous eye scans or reports.

  4. Plan for dilation

    Most first visits include dilating drops that blur vision for a few hours. It is safer not to drive yourself home.

  5. Stop contact lenses before a cataract consultation

    Lenses change the shape of the cornea and can affect the measurements used to choose your lens implant. Stop soft lenses at least 1 week before, and rigid (RGP) lenses at least 2–3 weeks before, unless the clinic advises otherwise. Bring your glasses instead.

Sudden vision loss, a painful red eye, or an eye injury? Do not wait for a clinic day. Go to the nearest emergency department or call 1669.
About

Dr. Thanapong Somkijrungroj

Dr Somkijrungroj graduated from Phramongkutklao College of Medicine, Bangkok, in 2004, served as a medical officer in the Royal Thai Army (2004–2007) and completed his ophthalmology residency at Rajavithi Hospital, Bangkok (2007–2010, best resident award). He trained in retina and vitreous at Chulalongkorn University (2011–2012) and, as an international fellow of the Francis I. Proctor Foundation, University of California, San Francisco, in uveitis and in medical cornea and external disease (2013–2014). He joined the faculty of Chulalongkorn University in 2012 and has led its uveitis unit since; he trains two to three retina fellows each year and opened the university’s uveitis fellowship in 2017.

His practice spans advanced and complicated cataract surgery, uveitis, and medical and surgical retina. His research interests include presbyopia-correcting IOL optics and digital reading performance with multifocal lenses, immediate sequential bilateral cataract surgery, imaging in uveitis and retina, diagnostic tests for uveitis, CMV keratouveitis, ocular Behçet disease and infectious uveitis, and intravitreal drug-delivery devices.

He founded the Chula–KKU–Proctor–UCSF (CKPU) conference (first meeting January 2017), heads the information technology committees of the Royal College of Ophthalmologists of Thailand (2020–present) and the Thailand Ocular Immunology and Inflammation Society (2014–present), and served on the committee of the Thai Retina Society (2018–2020). He is an APACRS Certified Educator (2026) and a regular faculty member at APACRS, APAO, APVRS, ESCRS, IOIS and the Royal College meetings.

In 2026 he created the IOL Optics Atlas (iolatlas.com), an online resource for the lifelong education of ophthalmologists in intraocular lens optics.

Magazine featureคนต้นแบบ · Role Model column · May–June issue

A role model for the next generation of eye doctors

Dr. Thananop, then a fourth-year medical student at Chulalongkorn University, names Dr. Thanapong as the teacher who inspired him to become an ophthalmologist. He describes watching Dr. Thanapong diagnose a rare genetic retinal disease by adapting how OCT imaging was used, and the lesson that stayed with him: put the patient first. The feature also covers Dr. Thanapong's own view of ophthalmology as a blend of medicine, surgery and innovation.

Lifelong education

IOL Optics Atlas

An online atlas Dr. Thanapong created for the lifelong education of ophthalmologists. It explains how intraocular lenses work, from optical principle to defocus curve.

For ophthalmologists

Intraocular lens optics, computed and sourced

Eighteen interactive pages, computed in the browser: lenses classified by optical principle and depth of field, simulated defocus curves, optical bench, night halos, toric alignment, biometers and IOL formulas. Every value is linked to its source and graded by level of evidence.

  • 37IOL models
  • 38IOL formulas
  • 14optical biometers
  • 1,000+references

Built for teaching, with a Present mode for lecture slides. It is not a substitute for manufacturer bench data or clinical trials, and it is not meant for patients to choose a lens.

Open the IOL Optics Atlas
